many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

# ARC: 3x3 ring markers crossing full 2-lines

## Trigger
A grid contains one or more 3x3 square-ring markers: eight 3s around a central 2. One or more complete straight lines of 2s (horizontal or vertical) run through the marker center(s), with other parallel 2-lines elsewhere in the grid.

## Transformation
1. Keep the grid dimensions unchanged. Preserve the original 3-ring markers.
2. For each marker, determine the direction perpendicular to its full 2-line: a horizontal 2-line through the marker center implies a vertical center-axis projection; a vertical 2-line implies a horizontal projection.
3. Extend that center axis through the full grid in both directions. Recolor zeros along the axis to 1. Leave existing 2s on the axis as 2 (the projection crosses, but does not erase, the line).
4. At each crossing of that projected axis with a parallel full 2-line, stamp the 3x3 ring pattern: recolor the eight surrounding cells to 1, while retaining the central intersection cell as 2. This includes replacing neighboring cells of the 2-line itself with 1. Do not restrict the stamp to zeros; the neighboring 2s are intentionally overwritten.
5. Leave all unrelated cells unchanged. If multiple projections overlap, retain the original 3 markers and central 2s; otherwise use 1 for the projected/stamped cells.

## Demonstration-derived checks
- With horizontal 2-lines and a ring centered on one, the 1-axis is vertical. At the crossing of another horizontal 2-line, the intersection stays 2, while the adjacent cells on that horizontal line become 1; rows immediately above/below also get the 1-ring sides.
- With vertical 2-lines, transpose the rule: the 1-axis is horizontal, and at each vertical-line crossing the central cell stays 2 while the cells immediately above/below it are recolored 1.
- A 3-ring is already the source marker, not a cue to fill its entire row/column indiscriminately. Extend only its center axis and add 1-rings at line crossings.

## Pitfalls
- Do not preserve every 2 in the surrounding 3x3 crossing stamp. Only its center remains 2; the eight ring positions become 1, even when they originally belonged to a perpendicular/parallel 2-line.
- Do not paint the whole grid, the whole row/column band, or only the empty cells in a crossing stamp.
- The center axis may intersect several full lines; repeat the ring stamp at each crossing.
- Verify row/column indexing and preserve untouched portions of the input exactly.
